findings.finding: Customer go-lives that feed Q2 recurring revenue are company-confirmed: Northeast Georgia Medical Center (~850,000 exams/yr) live on Sectra One Cloud in Q4 2025/26, Meritus Health (~257,000 exams/yr) live in Q2, Emory fully migrated in Q1, Scotland national rollout started -- supporting continued high CRR growth (Q1 +75%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Strong recurring/EBIT prints have been sold: Q2 2025/26 EBIT 188.6m vs 136m FactSet consensus, stock -2.35% (2025-12-12); Q1 2026/27 +61% EBIT, gapped +3.2% and closed -0.1% (2026-09-04).

findings.why_not_priced: Company-stated, so analysts have it; the unknown is the pace. Segment is ~12% of group sales (R12 SEK 449m of ~3.7bn), so net of the rest of the company it is small; Imaging IT must hold its margin for this to show.

findings.finding: Tough EBIT comparator plus company-flagged cost ramp: year-ago Q2 EBIT 188.6m at a 22.2% margin was boosted by a customer's compensation for project delays (amount undisclosed), and the CEO said in Q1 that added US resources 'will entail increased costs before we see the corresponding revenue' -- so headline y/y EBIT growth falls from +61% in Q1 to low teens or less, with margin likely down y/y.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin/cost commentary drove the Dec 2025 sell-off despite a beat ('Kostnader kommer satta press pa bolaget', efn.se); Sep 2026 gap-up faded to flat.
findings.why_not_priced: Analysts know the comp, but Swedish wire headlines (Finwire/Borsvarlden/Placera) lead with y/y change, and a low or negative y/y EBIT headline on a stock 13% up over 60 days is the kind of line this name has sold. If priced, the snippet consensus would be below Q1 run-rate; at EPS 0.89 it is above it.
